cells.tense: You are here with the pen in your hand, choosing direction out of the full spread of what you feel.
cells.act: let the feeling settle into its own depth
cells.ask: Pick one feeling that's already here. Stay with it, no task attached, until it settles to its own depth, then put it down.
cells.core:
You can feel the whole spread of what's around you and point yourself anyway. When you choose a direction, nothing gets left out of it — what you feel about the people in it, what you're afraid of, what you want — all of it comes along. The pick holds because the feeling under it has gone quiet, not because nothing is moving.

That quiet is paid for. You sit with what's already in you long enough for it to settle, and the settled feeling is what lets you say this, not that, and mean it. Let one feeling reach its own depth this week. Then aim again, with that depth resting under the aim.
cells.sheetLine: You choose from all of it, not half.
cells.verb: feeling the whole of what connects, with nothing left out
cells.place: choosing which way to point yourself

cells.tense: You will need the whole picture settled before you move, and the settling will not arrive in time.
cells.act: define the seed of what will be built, in one line
cells.ask: Before you pick, write one line naming the seed of what you're building. Then choose from that line, not from every feeling you can feel.
cells.core:
On the way to choosing, the whole spread is being checked first. Every feeling has to be accounted for before a direction is picked, and the pick keeps waiting for an accounting that won't finish. The waiting looks like care. It reads from outside as someone at a door with the key already in hand.

Nothing is missing from what you feel. What's missing is the first line of the form. One sentence naming what you want the thing to be gives your direction somewhere to stand, and the rest of the feeling can stay true without having to vote. Say the line. Then choose, aware that plenty is still unsettled.

cells.tense: You are still at a door already behind you, and the whole spread hasn't been picked up.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: Something this week will pull at you before you've decided what it's for — a sound, a person, an idea. Catch it early, and hold off on sorting it.
cells.core:
There's a direction you already passed through, and it's still being chosen somewhere. What you feel is real, but the whole spread isn't reaching the hand that points — the spark gets caught only after it's been sorted, and sorting isn't picking. The ability to say this, not that is intact. It just isn't being let near anything fresh.

Fresh is cheaper than direction. Catch one thing this week that pulls at you and keep it unlabeled, with no plan and no verdict on whether it matters. The point isn't to commit. The point is to let one spark exist in your attention before it turns into a decision. What you catch tells you wanting is still running.

cells.tense: Right now the pen is moving without anyone claiming to hold it, and a direction is being taken anyway.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: The next time something in you is sure of the right move — small, private, unwitnessed — do it that same day, and take the credit inside yourself.
cells.core:
You are pointing yourself, carefully, in ways credited to something else — the situation, the timing, what had to happen. The aim is real and it's good. What's missing is the name on it: no one, including you, is calling the direction deliberate. The cost is that your own aim stays something you can't trust on purpose.

Start smaller than a principle. When something in you is sure of the right move in a small case, do it that day, and let yourself be the one who says so. You don't have to announce it to anyone. You do have to own that the compass moved and your hand was on it.
cells.sheetLine: You're steering it. The credit says otherwise.

attempts.check: The record's Full Awareness of Felt Connection is wholeness of feeling, not any claim that the person has finished something or closed a chapter — my drafts pushed toward completion-as-end and had to be pulled back to the rainbow of feeling, not the rainbow's end. A reader could reasonably hear 'the whole of it' as an ending being announced, so the cores name fullness that keeps deepening rather than arrival, and the asks never promise the feeling will stay. The ask in each cell is the partner's own action and does not depend on my read of the signature being right; if the read above is wrong, the person still walks away with one small act of their own medicine. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'the whole of it' — it saves me explaining the rainbow; I've written it as 'the whole spread of it' and let the image carry, not the summary.

A reader could hear 'the whole spread' as an ending being announced; each core keeps the feeling as a wide present, and Reverie's balanced face — recognition that honors self and other, connection without fusion — is what the growth ask is for, not a promise the feeling stays. Each ask is one of the medicine's own listed acts done small in Will, and stands whether or not my read of the signature is right. The sentence that serves me more than them was 'the whole of it' — I've replaced it with 'the whole spread of what you feel' and let the picture carry it.
